info.name: Hookbase MCP — HTTP Transport
info.description:
Exercises the Hookbase MCP server's remote **Streamable HTTP** transport (JSON-RPC 2.0) directly, without an MCP client.

- Base URL: `https://mcp.hookbase.app`. Single endpoint `POST /mcp` for all JSON-RPC calls; `GET /health` for liveness.
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer whr_...` (set the `api_key` collection variable). Optional multi-org disambiguation via `X-Hookbase-Org-Id` (set the `org_id` collection variable) — applied automatically by this collection's pre-request script.
- Supported JSON-RPC methods: `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `notifications/cancelled`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`. There is **no** `resources/*` or `prompts/*` support over HTTP — those only exist on the stdio transport.
- Every tool call response wraps the tool's actual output as a JSON-encoded **string** at `result.content[0].text` (plus `result.isError`) — parse that string to get the real payload, it is not returned as raw nested JSON.
- Folders below mirror the 123 tools exposed by `tools/list`, one example `tools/call` request per tool. Fill in the empty `*_id` collection variables after creating a resource (e.g. run "Sources > Create Source", then paste the returned id into `source_id`) so the rest of that folder's requests work without editing the body.

exec: // Send X-Hookbase-Org-Id on every request when org_id is set (for multi-org API keys).

item.name: Setup & Transport
item.description: Transport-level JSON-RPC methods implemented by the HTTP MCP handler: initialize, notifications/initialized, ping, and tools/list. There is no resources/* or prompts/* support over HTTP (those exist only in the stdio transport) — calling them here returns a -32601 Method not found error.

request.description: Liveness probe. Returns plain-text "ok" with no auth required.
First call of a session. Negotiates protocol version and returns serverInfo/capabilities. Does not require the API key to be valid yet — auth is only checked on tools/call.
Fire-and-forget lifecycle notification after initialize. No "id" field (per JSON-RPC, notifications get no response) — expect HTTP 202 with an empty body.
Basic liveness check over the JSON-RPC channel. Returns an empty result object.
Enumerate all available tools with their JSON Schema input definitions. Identical response for every request (cached per isolate).
